# Job Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 420r–420v

---

**12:1** And-answered Iyyov [Job] and-said:

**12:2** "Truly [omnam] you [are] the-people [am], and-with-you will-die wisdom [chokhmah]. **12:3** Also I [have] a-heart [levav] like-you; not [am] I falling [nofel] from-you; and-with whom [are] there-not [things] like-these?

**12:4** A-laughingstock [sechoq] to-his-neighbor I-have-become — [one who] calls to-God [eloah] and-he-answers-him — a-laughingstock [is] the-righteous [tsaddiq], the-blameless [tamim]. **12:5** A-torch [lappid] despised [buz] in-the-thought [le'ashut] of-the-one-at-ease [sha'anan], prepared [nakun] for-the-ones-whose-foot [raglei] slips [mo'adei].

**12:6** At-peace [yishlayu] [are] the-tents of-robbers [shodedim], and-security [betuchot] [belongs] to-the-ones-who-provoke God [margizei el], to-the-one-who-brings God in-his-hand [beyado].

**12:7** But-indeed [ve-ulam] ask [she'al] now the-beasts [behemot] and-they-will-teach-you [vetorekha], and-the-birds of-the-heavens [of ha-shamayim] and-they-will-tell-you [vetaged-lakh]. **12:8** Or speak [siach] to-the-earth [la-arets] and-it-will-teach-you, and-the-fish of-the-sea [dagei ha-yam] will-recount [visapru] to-you. **12:9** Who does-not know [lo yada] among-all these that the-hand of-YHWH has-done this? **12:10** [He] in-whose-hand [beyado] [is] the-soul [nefesh] of-every living-thing [kol chai], and-the-spirit [ruach] of-all flesh [basar] of-man [ish].

**12:11** Does-not the-ear [ozen] test [tivhan] words [millin], as-the-palate [chekh] tastes [yit'am] food [okhel] for-itself? **12:12** With-the-aged [bishishim] [is] wisdom [chokhmah], and-[in] length of-days [orekh yamim] [is] understanding [tevunah].

**12:13** With-him [imo] [are] wisdom and-might [gevurah]; to-him [are] counsel [etsah] and-understanding [tevunah]. **12:14** Behold, he-tears-down [yahros] and-it-will-not be-rebuilt [yibaneh]; he-shuts [yisgor] upon a-man and-it-will-not be-opened [yipatach]. **12:15** Behold, he-withholds [ya'atsor] the-waters [mayim] and-they-dry-up [veyivashu]; and-he-sends-them-out [vishaleichem] and-they-overturn [yahapekhu] [the] earth [erets].

**12:16** With-him [are] strength [oz] and-sound-wisdom [tushiyah]; to-him [belong] the-one-who-errs [shoggeg] and-the-one-who-leads-astray [mashgeh]. **12:17** He-leads counselors [yo'atsim] away stripped [sholal], and-judges [shofetim] he-makes-foolish [yeholel]. **12:18** The-bond [musar] of-kings he-opens [pittach], and-he-binds [vaya'asor] a-loincloth [ezor] on-their-loins [bematnehem].

**12:19** He-leads priests [kohanim] away stripped [sholal], and-the-established [etanim] he-overthrows [yesallef]. **12:20** He-removes [mesir] speech [safah] from-the-trusted [la-ne'emanim], and-the-discernment [ta'am] of-elders [zeqenim] he-takes-away [yiqqach].

**12:21** He-pours [shofekh] contempt [buz] upon nobles [nedivim], and-the-belt [meziach] of-the-mighty [afiqim] he-loosens [rippah]. **12:22** He-uncovers [megalleh] deep-things [amuqot] from-the-darkness [me-choshekh], and-he-brings-out [vayotse] to-the-light [la-or] deep-shadow [tsalmaveth].

**12:23** He-makes-great [mashgi] the-nations [goyim] and-he-destroys-them [va-ye'abdem]; he-spreads-out [shoteiach] the-nations and-he-leads-them-away [vayanechem]. **12:24** He-removes [mesir] the-heart [lev] of-the-heads [rashei] of-the-people [am] of-the-earth [ha-arets], and-he-makes-them-wander [vayat'em] in-a-waste [tohu] [where there is] no way [lo darekh]. **12:25** They-grope [yemasheshu] [in] darkness [choshekh] and-not light [lo or], and-he-makes-them-stagger [vayat'em] like-the-drunkard [kashikkor]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "with you will die wisdom":** Biting sarcasm. Job mocks his friends as though they held a monopoly on wisdom — when they die, all knowledge will perish with them.

**v.9 — "the hand of YHWH":** This is the only occurrence of the divine name YHWH in the poetic dialogue of Job (ch. 3-37). Most scholars consider it original, though some suspect scribal assimilation from Isaiah 41:20.

**v.16 — shoggeg/mashgeh:** These paired terms ("the one who errs" and "the one who causes error") emphasize God's sovereignty over both the deceived and the deceiver — a bold theological claim.

**v.22 — tsalmaveth:** Traditionally "shadow of death," likely a compound of *tselem* (shadow) + *maveth* (death), though some parse it as an intensified form of *tsalmut* (deep darkness).

*— EMET*
